chosen.description:
The bodyweight squat can be one of the most functional and fundamental strength exercises out there. This basic squat movement builds hip and ankle mobility, and resiliency of the legs. Here is a 30 day plan for increasing your squat strength, endurance, and mobility.

Lets get back to basics and challenge ourselves with this 30-day squat plan. We all know that squats are a basic fundamental exercise, but are we really executing them right? We want to focus on quality, not quantity. It's not just about going up and down so many times. It's about really activating our legs and our core for a focused range of motion. Even if you're a pro at squats, or even if you're using resistance, challenge yourself to this simple 30-day challenge to see improvements in your endurance and mobility.

candidates.title: Squat (Bodyweight) | Fit for the 500 | IU Health Sports Performance
candidates.description:
IU Health Sports Performance and Andretti Autosport are teaming up to get fit for the Indianapolis 500! Each week, we'll post a new fitness challenge and then help you put it all together at the end.

Week 3 Challenge: Strength coach, Tavio Henson, shows an Andretti Autosport pit crew member how to do a correct body squat. This exercise engages a number of muscle groups and will help you strengthen your core and lower body, including your glute max, hamstrings, quads, abdominals and erector spinae group.

Remember to keep your knees over your toes and weight on your heels. You want to sit back with your hips and keep your back upright and straight.

For this week's challenge, do as many squats as you can. Then add 10 more the next day. Post your progress by using #Fit4the500!

To learn more about strength and conditioning, visit http://www.iuhealth.org/sports-performance.

candidates.title: Leg exercise - How to bodyweight squat
candidates.description:
1. Stand tall with feet slightly wider than hip-width distance apart, feet slightly turned out.
2. Roll your shoulders and down away from the ears. This will help you to maintain a straight spine.
3. Extend your arms out in front of you with your palms facing down. Your arms should be in a position where they are parallel to the ground.
4. Look straight ahead and take a deep breathe in and tighten your ab muscles. Then bend your knees and sink your hips back while lowering your hips towards the floor until it sinks just below the knees. Try to keep a straight spine and tight core throughout the whole movement.
5. Stay in this position briefly, before straightening your legs and exploding back up to standing position, and then exhale.
6. Repeat as many repetitions required.
